title: What is Tray Embedded? A 2026 Guide
summary: Tray embedded provides a managed infrastructure for software companies to offer native integrations without building and maintaining custom API connectors.
body_markdown:
## How tray embedded architecture functions production-side


Tray Embedded functions as a multi-tenant orchestration layer that abstracts API complexity into a visual logic builder for rapid deployment.


By decoupling the workflow logic from the underlying code, engineering teams can offload the maintenance of individual connectors to the platform while retaining control over the data mapping.


### The Integration Manager and low-code builder


Developers publish master workflow templates to specific customer groups through the Integration Manager, which serves as the centralized version control and distribution hub. This structural separation is critical because the average business now manages 144 SaaS applications according to[Vertice](https://www.vertice.one/insights/saas-apps-per-business) .


A manual approach to updating individual customer scripts isn't scalable. Since this count has climbed steadily from 131 in June 2025 and 138 in March 2026, the builder uses a "drag-and-drop" interface. It allows non-engineers to adjust field mappings without touching the core codebase.


The risk of this abstraction is that the vendor owns the rights to the logic you build on their infrastructure.


Activepieces provides a different legal foundation by publishing its core under an MIT licence, which you can verify by reading the LICENSE file in the activepieces/activepieces repository.


This ensures that the code powering your integrations remains yours to run, fork, or embed regardless of the vendor's future pricing changes.


### Presenting the interface to end users


The end-user interacts with these workflows through a Config Wizard, a pre-built UI component that you embed into your application via an iframe or a JavaScript SDK.


This wizard guides the user through the necessary authentication steps and configuration settings required to activate a Solution Instance.


By using this embedded component, your team avoids building custom frontend forms for every new integration. The wizard dynamically generates fields based on the workflow requirements, allowing users to map their own data or set specific toggle options.


### Handling end-user authentication with Auth Slots


Unique credentials for each customer's third-party services are stored in secure, encrypted containers called Auth Slots.


By using these slots, a developer writes the integration logic once using a placeholder. The system can dynamically inject the correct OAuth tokens or API keys at runtime.


This architecture ensures that sensitive customer data remains isolated within their specific environment, preventing cross-tenant data leaks during high-volume executions.


### Merlin AI for automated workflow generation


Merlin AI utilizes advanced reasoning models like Claude Sonnet 5.5 to translate natural language requirements into functional step-by-step automation logic. This reduces the initial build time for complex branching paths.


1. Input natural language prompt
2. Merlin generates workflow logic
3. Engineer reviews/edits visual steps
4. Deploy to Integration Manager


Describing the desired outcome allows a team to prototype a new connector in minutes. Once the engineer validates the logic, they push it to the production environment for immediate end-user activation.
